newsitem.title: USA: O.J. appearance at golf tournament draws protest.
newsitem.headline: O.J. appearance at golf tournament draws protest.

text.p: A group of protesters carrying signs reading "butcherer" and "liar" demonstrated in this posh Miami suburb Friday against the appearance of former football star O.J. Simpson at a celebrity golf tournament.

Simpson, who was cleared of murder charges in the 1994 knife slayings of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ron Goldman but later found responsible for their deaths in a civil trial, played at the annual Celebrity Golf Challenge to raise funds for sickle cell anaemia research.
He was not among the invited celebrities but paid an entry fee to play. Among the celebrities scheduled to play were director Spike Lee and actor Denzel Washington.
About a dozen protesters lined up behind police barricades outside the golf course, waving placards to protest his appearance. One sign read "Real Men Don't Hit Women."
"O.J. Simpson shouldn't be out walking the streets and we're not happy to have him on ours," one protester told local media.
"I wasn't happy at all about the fact that he was going to be joining other celebrities. I don't see him as a celebrity," said another.
Simpson teed off despite the protest and said he was not bothered by the demonstrators.
"This is America. They have a right to protest," Simpson told CBS affiliate WFOR.
In a Miami radio interview Thursday, Simpson urged the relatives of Goldman and his ex-wife to press the Los Angeles Police Department to reopen the investigation in order to find the real killers.

Simpson, who was slapped with a $33.5 million judgment by the civil trial jury, was seen during the weekend with his children at a trendy hotel and eatery in Miami Beach's modelling mecca, South Beach.
